5701.full: κακουχέω, -ῶ (κακόν, ἔχω), [in LXX: 3Ki.2:26 11:39 (עָנָה pi., hith.)* ;] to ill-treat, hurt, torment: pass. ptcp., Heb.11:37 13:3.† (AS)

5702.full: 1. ill-minded, malicious, malignant , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. imprudent, thoughtless, heedless , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: to adorn oneself, make oneself fine
to make a display, shew off
5705.full: 1. properly, to make the face beautiful; hence, to beautify, embellish , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., κεκαλλωπισμέναι τὸ χρῶμα, i. e. painted, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid. to adorn oneself, make oneself fine or smart , (Plato Philosophus): metaphorically to pride oneself in or on a thing, τινι or ἐπί τινι (Plato Philosophus):—;absolute to make a display, shew off , of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to be coy, play the prude , τινι or πρός τινα towards another, (Plato Philosophus); with infinitive, κ. παραιτεῖσθαι to affect to deprecate, (Plutarch) (ML)

Χριστόν, Php.1:17; pass., Php.1:18. __2. to denounce (Xen., al.); (for comparison with ἀγγέλλω, ἀναγ-, ἀπαγ-, see Westc. on 1Jn.1:5; and cf. προ-καταγγέλλω).† (AS)

s: to receive back, take home again
5716.full: 1. Dep. 2. to receive, admit , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. to receive back, take home again , (Isaeus Orator): —;aor1 passive καταδεχθῆναι in passive sense, (Lucian) (ML)

5718.full: 1. in the mind or thoughts , (Odyssey by Homer); μηδέ τί τοι θάνατος κατ. ἔστω let not death sit heavy on thy heart , (Iliad by Homer) 2. according to one's mind, satisfactory , (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

5724.full: to roll down :—;Pass. to be rolled down or thrown off , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to be flattered, be open to flattery
